subject: Dedicated SKU queue stability and addendum request
messages:
From: Maria Vance <maria.vance@mistelcorp.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@mistelcorp.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated pool: nightly queueing spikes and requested accommodation

Hi Nikhil,

Quick note from our SRE team: during last night's batch window (~02:00-04:00 ET) we saw sustained queueing on the reserved GPU pool that caused a ~600ms tail latency increase for our real-time endpoints and about ~18% drop in throughput for heavy prompt workloads. That crossover exacted visible downstream effects on customer-facing jobs.

We're on a reserved-dedicated plan and expected the usual isolation, so this surprised us. Can Redwood confirm whether this is expected behavior during rolling maintenance or capacity rebalancing? If this is operationally unavoidable, we need to discuss either a temporary carveout (nightly concurrency headroom) or an SLA addendum that explicitly describes allowable windowed variance and remedies.

I've attached the perf logs slice and a short telemetry CSV that shows the spike mapping to the window (perf_logs_oct29.gz, nightly-telemetry-sample.csv).

High level asks:
- Root cause and confirmation of whether this was a preemption/eviction event or batching-induced backlog.
- Proposal for a short-term mitigation (scheduled capacity bump, queue priority lanes, or reserved burst tokens).
- Contractual wording for a one-off addendum covering scheduled batch windows, backstop credits, and predictable failover behavior.

We're mid-procurement on a larger reserved commitment and need this clarified before signing the renewal.

Thanks — appreciate a quick triage.

Maria Vance
Head of Platform Ops, MistelCorp
maria.vance@mistelcorp.com
Attachment: perf_logs_oct29.gz (log), nightly-telemetry-sample.csv (csv)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Maria Vance <maria.vance@mistelcorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: nightly queueing spikes and requested accommodation

Maria — thanks for the data and flag. I've pulled the perf bundle and started an internal triage. Initial notes:

- We see a small maintenance-related rolling restart that coincided with the window. The restart should not cause preemption of reserved GPUs, but it can cause short-lived overload on the local scheduler while nodes rejoin (we're seeing backlog spikes in the 30s-120s range).
- The telemetry slice you sent lines up with a burst of queued requests that matches a large batched job from your account at 02:13. That batching pattern increased KV cache misses and forced more frequent kernel launch overhead across the pool.

We've looped in our Dedicated SLA working group (cc: Laura, Ben). Proposed immediate actions:
1) Short-term: schedule a 20% capacity burst for MistelCorp during the 02:00-04:30 ET window for the next 14 days while we validate batching optimizations (no billing delta during the trial).
2) Medium-term: propose an addendum to your Dedicated contract that explicitly defines: allowable nightly variance, guaranteed burst tokens (X tokens/day), and a remediation credit schedule if tail latency exceeds agreed thresholds for more than Y consecutive windows.
3) Technical: we'll ship a per-tenant queue-priority policy to ensure interactive endpoints keep a higher priority over large batch jobs during isolated windows. That will require a short config change on your side to classify request types.

Next steps: Ben will draft the addendum terms and Laura will coordinate the SRE runbook for the priority policy. Can you share a short list of the batch job identifiers or the service name that runs at 02:13 so we can correlate programmatically? Also confirm whether you want the burst window to be recurring or limited to the next two weeks for validation.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Capacity Solutions — Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Attachment: n/a
From: Maria Vance <maria.vance@mistelcorp.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@mistelcorp.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:09:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: nightly queueing spikes and requested accommodation

Thanks, Nikhil. Appreciate the quick triage and the trial capacity offer.

Service names: outlier-batch-worker and bulk-encoder-2 (both under ops@mistelcorp.com). Those run once nightly to refresh models and produce large embedding batches; they do send high-concurrency requests over a 20–40 minute window. We can add a header to mark them as batch traffic if that helps.

For the addendum: recurring night window is preferable (we run nightly), but we are open to a 30-day validation first. Two items we need in the addendum language: clear measurement baseline (how tail latency is computed; percentile and sample size), and a credit stair-step tied to consecutive missed windows (not just aggregate monthly).

Also please include a clear fallback policy: if Redwood cannot meet the burst guarantee for >3 consecutive nights we need an automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant in another region with clear RTO and data handling clauses.

I'll review any proposed draft and loop in procurement if numbers change.

Maria
Attachment: none
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Vance <maria.vance@mistelcorp.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: nightly queueing spikes and requested accommodation

Maria — looping in the contractual specifics. Per Nikhil's ask I've sketched a short addendum and a fallback runbook:

- Measurement baseline: 95th and 99th tail latency computed over a 5-minute rolling window; sample must be at least 1,000 tokens or 200 requests per window (whichever is larger).
- Credit schedule: first missed window -> technical incident review (no credit); second consecutive missed window -> 10% monthly usage credit pro-rated for the affected windows; third consecutive missed window -> 25% credit and optional termination right for the nightly-carveout portion.
- Burst tokens: 10,000 free tokens per night for 30 days trial; then 5,000/day baseline included under the addendum. Additional burst billed at agreed reserved overage rates.
- Fallback policy: automatic regional failover only if Redwood confirms capacity < 80% for your reserved pool for >4 hours and after mutual confirmation triggers. Failover will spin a hosted-compatible variant in the east-us region with encrypted transit and at-rest controls; data access logging will be enabled and any cross-region data egress will be logged for audit.

Action items:
- Maria/procurement: confirm the trial window cadence (recurring nightly or 30-day trial).
- Maria/ops: mark the batch workers with the new header so we can classify them and test the priority lane logic.
- Nikhil/ops: schedule the burst capacity and coordinate the config rollout (ETA within 48 hours).

I'll place the draft addendum in the shared drive and send a DocuSign link once we have procurement sign-off.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Contracts — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed_addendum_draft.pdf
